Purpose: Establish the city silhouette, vertical class divide and borough geography.
Design notes: The floating borough captions are removed and the five-district layout is preserved. Small billboard copy was distorted by generation and needs lettering cleanup; architecture and blue-mana rail connections are ready as concept references.

Purpose: Show how the megacity overwhelms a person at street level.
Design notes: Strong distinct 2:3 upward street-canyon composition: tiny street residents and tram, towering glass blocks, smog shaft, wet pavement and physical blue-mana utility lines. Architecture and graphic-novel treatment match the selected city anchor. Main NEONIX — ONE CITY, MANY HEARTS lettering is readable and correct. A prominent orange sign at lower right prints F7B32B, an unintended palette code; remove or abstract that specific sign. Other incidental abstract markings are not treated as lore errors.
Continuity notes: The dramatic vertical scale and street-level tram are useful new coverage. Preserve routed blue technology and the old-brick bases beneath glass towers.

Purpose: Show the public connective tissue between the five boroughs.
Design notes: Distinct practical rail-concourse view with a train, connected platforms, elevated pedestrian circulation, warm stalls, patched concrete, glass towers, distant crystal highland and industrial chimneys. Mixed adult commuters and blue conduits bring the city to human scale. Crisp ink/cel rendering stays consistent with the anchor. No material scene or anatomy error found.
Continuity notes: Keep the platform/train scale, protected passenger paths and blue routes physically attached to the rail infrastructure. Distant district landmarks are continuity cues, not a new fixed street map.

Purpose: Explain the characteristic blue-mana infrastructure at human scale.
Design notes: Successful environmental technology close-up: glass inspection cylinder, bright blue contained mana, worn brass clamps, steel gantry, connected street lamp and a technician with physical blue-linked cyberware. Distant trains and towers retain city context. The image is materially distinct from both aerial and concourse scenes and reads as a physical utility installation rather than a diagram. No material issue found.
Continuity notes: Retain transparent inspection sleeves, weathered brass/steel fasteners and contained blue flow as the city infrastructure vocabulary.

Purpose: Contrast high clean terraces with the dense polluted city below.
Design notes: Night palette, ivory balcony arches, quiet upper-city residents and blue transit lines are consistent with Neonix. However, the background is essentially the same aerial anchor composition with foreground balconies added; tower, factory, monument and crystal-spire placements remain nearly pixel-for-pixel alike. This functions as an atmosphere variant rather than the requested genuinely different upper-city viewpoint. Recompose from within the highland terrace, looking down and outward across the city, while preserving geographically plausible relationships. No character anatomy blocker found.
Continuity notes: Preserve borough silhouettes and rail language, but do not freeze the southeast aerial's screen-space positions after changing the camera.

Purpose: Establish the borough as ancient stone integrated with advanced glass.
Design notes: Clear match to the raised garden terrace: pale stone and smooth white/glass spires, grown wood arches, silver filigree balustrades, stepped roof gardens and a faceted conservatory dome. Clean sunset air contrasts visibly with the hazier neon city below. Few tall adult elves, quiet lantern drones and restrained blue runes routed through roots/walkways keep the scene refined and inhabited. Strong architectural ink/cel treatment; no trash, horror crowd, intrusive text or material departure requiring correction.
Continuity notes: Carry forward ivory/sage/pale-gold materials, grown timber arch supports, curved carved terraces with filigree rails, blue root/path channels and the distant faceted dome. Preserve high-ground views over polluted lower Neonix and spacious occupancy.

Purpose: Show the required street approach and old foundations beneath new construction.
Design notes: Distinct spacious approach with living-wood gateway arches, blue rune paths/roots, a modern glass tower directly above old pale masonry, planted terraces and a quiet luxury vehicle. Tall adult residents, clear air and pale ivory/sage/gold colors match the anchor. ELVEN HEIGHTS — PRIVATE RESIDENTIAL is correctly legible. The futuristic vehicle strengthens the contemporary city reading. No material issue found.
Continuity notes: Use the grown arch shape, pale carved foundations, fine silver details and glass/stone connection as shared borough vocabulary.

Purpose: Reveal the borough public-space language at a more intimate scale.
Design notes: A new garden-court composition shows stepped seating areas, restrained planting, glass lift/tower surfaces, grown wood framing and a silver-filagree balcony pavilion. Sparse adult residents and clear sunset air retain the privileged quiet of the anchor. Blue mana follows the living wood instead of forming an uncontrolled aura. Distinct useful public-space coverage, with no material issue found.
Continuity notes: Preserve curving pale-stone terraces, grown timber supports, silver rails and the lower smoggy city beyond. The unnamed background residents do not establish new NPC identities.

Purpose: Specify the material transition that makes the borough recognizable.
Design notes: Successful material-scale detail: large living root with engraved blue routes meets pale ancient stone and a precise modern glass wall with silver fittings. Abstract ornamental elvish plaque, distant terrace figures and the city below retain scale and place. The close view adds clear construction detail without becoming an infographic or plain fantasy forest. No material issue found.
Continuity notes: The rune/root/glass junction can guide later architectural details. Abstract script is decoration rather than newly approved language or lore.

Purpose: Test the same design at night while retaining privilege and isolation.
Design notes: Dusk lighting, lantern drones, blue paths, clean high air and the faceted dome stay consistent with the anchor. The composition is almost exactly the original terrace view with people moved and a few larger lanterns added, rather than the planned eye-level journey along an elevated planted footbridge. It is a useful lighting variant but does not provide a distinct fifth spatial concept. Reframe from the footbridge with foreground bridge circulation and a different relationship to the spires.
Continuity notes: Keep the anchor's material and landmark language while changing actual camera position. Do not propagate the duplicate framing as a second established viewpoint.

Purpose: Establish the borough main street and mixed architecture.
Design notes: Good lived-in street composition: preserved brick storefronts below glass-and-steel towers and balconies, wet pavement, central tram on blue rails, food carts and a busy mixed-species adult crowd. Compact bearded dwarves read as adults; several ordinary residents have distinct physically attached blue-mana cyberware. Teal, warm shop light and small red accents suit the borough. Material deviation is prominent extra signage: IMPLANT CLINIC, BLUE MANA, SHOP and multiple invented/gibberish shop labels appear beyond the approved CENTRAL AVE. Remove or abstract additional lettering while retaining the avenue sign and architecture.
Continuity notes: Preserve street-level brick shops and stalls, uneven maintenance, a central tram corridor, tall modern blocks and wet teal/amber reflections. Later views should remain busy and inclusive without adopting the extra generated shop names or the literal BLUE MANA sign.

Purpose: Show the required elevated view and how old blocks remain under the skyline.
Design notes: Distinct elevated rooftop/balcony view adds brick parapets, utility equipment and stacked domestic balconies above the market avenue. Teal towers, blue tram routes and warm stalls match the anchor, with readable CENTRAL AVE and IMPLANT CLINIC signs. The tram stays straight rather than turning, a minor brief omission. Useful new elevation and scale; no material blocker.

Purpose: Show daily life and the borough’s inclusive public culture.
Design notes: New street-level market under substantial brick viaduct arches, with a modern tram overhead, vendors, musicians and varied adult residents. Worn brick, teal glass, amber stalls and physical blue transit lines retain borough continuity. Clear public circulation and ordinary cyberware support the lived-in city. Unity Day pennants are absent, but the scene remains useful distinct coverage.

Purpose: Connect retained historic fabric to affordable everyday augmentation.
Design notes: Clear environmental detail of a frosted-glass implant clinic in an old brick corner, weathered brass pipes, abstract posters and two distinct adults. Brass prosthetic forearms carry blue links and the elf has a compact blue ocular interface. Architecture, restrained palette and graphic-novel linework match the anchor. No material issue found.

Purpose: Test atmosphere and street circulation from the opposite end of the avenue.
Design notes: Convincing rainy rush hour, warm food counter and blue-linked everyday cyberware, but the scene repeats the anchor's same street direction, tower silhouettes, overhead CENTRAL AVE bridge, storefront positions and several right-side patrons. It is a rain/foreground variant rather than the requested reverse street view. Recompose from the opposite direction with geographically plausible landmarks and a genuinely different street relationship.

Purpose: Establish industrial scale, worker life and the district silhouette.
Design notes: Heavy brick halls, riveted bridge beams, low wide factory volumes, massive chimneys and prominent carved knotwork lintels match. Furnace orange across soot-grey haze is balanced with blue mana inside utility pipes. Workers with lunch tins include mature broad dwarves and taller humans; practical work clothes and occasional cyberware fit an industrial district. The physical LOCAL 7 — SAFETY FIRST, ALWAYS signs match the requested wording. No material visual deviation found; the image reads as working urban industry rather than a medieval town.
Continuity notes: Retain the broad arched-roof iron halls, deep carved knotwork stone bands, heavy riveted freight structure, tall cylindrical chimneys and sparse blue utility routes. Carry the orange foundry glow through soot haze into later district views.

Purpose: Show the required intimate street approach between the factories.
Design notes: Distinct narrow workshop lane with heavy brick, knotwork lintels, riveted iron, steam vents, handcarts and massive chimneys. Compact mature dwarves and taller human workers read clearly; blue mana follows physical pipe runes and an ear interface. Rust, brass and furnace light match the anchor. No material issue found.

Purpose: Show the district as a lived-in place between work shifts.
Design notes: Useful shift-break scene with adult dwarf/human workers, sturdy benches, food counter, freight carts and rails behind yellow barriers. The distant roof/chimney composition closely copies the anchor, but the foreground supplies a distinct loading-and-lunch function. The broader elevated deck and gantry are exploratory architecture; verify their footprint before treating this as a fixed map. Material and blue-pipe continuity are strong.

Purpose: Define craftsmanship embedded in industrial technology.
Design notes: Successful close detail of stone knotwork beside a riveted pipe manifold, worn brass valves, inspection glass and narrow blue routes. Soot, condensation and orange furnace bounce retain the district palette; only a gloved worker hand enters for scale. Distinct technical/material coverage without an infographic or added lore.

Purpose: Show the same industrial district from the worker streets at another hour.
Design notes: Nearly exact repeat of the anchor overpass framing, chimney skyline, factory roofs and worker placements, with stronger distant furnace glow and a small added figure. It does not deliver a genuinely new fifth composition. Reframe from another point on the pedestrian overpass while retaining the industrial material language and plausible roof relationships; the before-dawn atmosphere alone is insufficient new coverage.

Purpose: Establish beautiful decay and a humane, inventive neighborhood.
Design notes: Distinct inhabited alley with stacked container homes, hanging walkways, cable bundles, laundry, murals, rain reflections and ordinary adult residents socializing. Magenta/violet/acid-green accents and blue routed utilities create beauty within decay; mutants remain people rather than horror figures. WE ARE NOT HIDING is correctly present. Material signage issue: additional large words and code-like text include BLUE, A8E83A, MUSIC ULT and FRINGE THEATRE plus other invented strings, whereas this view allowed only the mural wording and a recognizable unlettered theatre marquee. Remove or abstract the extra lettering; retain the environment and humane crowd.
Continuity notes: Keep container corrugations, suspended footbridges, laundry/cable layers, wall art, wet narrow paving and mixed warm doorways within violet/magenta nightlife. Preserve the theatre marquee silhouette without propagating unapproved text or printed palette codes.

Purpose: Show the required elevated view and the living structure behind the alley.
Design notes: Strong genuinely elevated composition with container homes, attached bridges, laundry, rooftop planting and ordinary varied mutant residents. Blue utilities and magenta/violet/acid-green pigments retain the anchor language. However the prominent central green sign literally prints A8E83A and other neon signs resemble palette codes. Replace the clear color-code lettering with abstract in-world marks; preserve the successful rooftop geometry.

Purpose: Show the borough as a functioning social space.
Design notes: Distinct three-alley pocket court with food stall, musician doorway, adult mixed-species neighbors and varied counter heights. Materials, bridges, murals and the welcoming lived-in tone are appropriate. The upper-right green vertical sign carries the inherited recognizable A8E83A palette-code lettering; abstract or remove that sign text. Other small invented-looking marks remain incidental, and no major anatomy issue is evident.

Purpose: Study the union of art, blue mana and patched urban material.
Design notes: Successful mural-work detail: magenta/violet paint remains separate from blue channels, the artist has a physical brass prosthetic with blue links, and repair wiring/brick/corrugated panels establish context. The background still prominently repeats the literal A8E83A color-code sign despite the v2 instruction to avoid printed palette values. Remove or abstract that sign; retain the mural, modest technology and humane street context.

Purpose: Explore circulation and layered social life from a second scale.
Design notes: Genuinely different elevated walkway view looks diagonally into the alley, with laundry and plants in foreground, bolted container homes, attached bridges, warm doorways and ordinary mutant neighbors below. Blue utility conduits stay physical, with magenta/green signage secondary. The crop and changed angle plausibly reinterpret the anchor; keep frontage/sign attachment geometry exploratory until a fixed alley map is established. No material blocker found.

Purpose: Establish the poorest borough with dignity and a visible relationship to the city.
Design notes: Strong match: crumbling concrete, rusted pipes, tarp roofs, boarded openings and dim grey-violet haze, with distant city towers barely visible. Sparse respirator-wearing adult residents carry supplies and help one another by a warm window; an anonymous ration cart reinforces daily life. Residents remain dignified and anatomically human, with no zombie or horror treatment and no imposed glowing/clouded-eye rule. Grey-blue utility lights are small and restrained. MASKS ON is the only prominent readable wording. No material deviation found.
Continuity notes: Preserve layered damaged walkways and stairs, repaired tarps/boards, dull rusted infrastructure, faint distant towers, dim grey-blue power points and isolated warm windows. Later views should show residents with agency and ordinary survival routines, not horror staging.

Purpose: Show the required street scale and survival routines.
Design notes: Dignified respirator-wearing ration queue, readable RATIONS TUES/FRI and MASKS ON signs, patched tarps and restrained grey-blue technology fit the brief. However the same anchor camera, building silhouettes and several residents are retained while its deep central drop is filled into a broad ground-level street. The left warm window/stair arrangement is also replaced by a serving entrance. Recompose a separate ration street or resolve this substantial spatial alteration explicitly.

Purpose: Give the borough a social space and practical agency.
Design notes: Repair table, coat mending, scrap sorting and water carrying communicate mutual care without horror; dim grey-blue salvage interfaces and the modest amber lamp are appropriate. The image reuses the anchor skyline and near-identical bordering buildings, then converts the ravine-side area into a wide courtyard and alters the left opening/stairs. Establish a genuinely separate courtyard viewpoint rather than silently rebuilding the anchor foreground. The inhabitants and repair props are useful.

Purpose: Study poverty through repaired infrastructure rather than grotesque bodies.
Design notes: Useful close environmental study of a patched lamp, mismatched metal junction, tied wiring, rain-streaked concrete, repair tools and a respirator beside an older seated resident. A thin desaturated blue cable route and warm doorway fit the subdued Gloomscape language. No imposed glowing-eye design or horror treatment. Background retains recognizable district forms while the lamp supplies a distinct subject.

Purpose: Show an alternate evening mood with recognizable inhabited buildings.
Design notes: Warm windows, restrained blue lamps, respirators and distant bright city lights convey the intended perseverance and deprivation. The viewpoint nevertheless remains almost exactly the anchor, including the ravine, building silhouettes, tarp stall and several same-position residents. It is an illumination variant rather than the requested wide reverse view. Move the camera to a distinct foreground footpath and preserve geographically plausible architecture.

Purpose: Establish quiet luxury and magical drinks.
Design notes: Entrance view establishes the curved white-stone bar, living-wood columns branching into a star-visible glass roof, floating glass orbs, small musician ensemble and calm elegant adult patrons. Ivory, pale gold and muted violet lighting give quiet luxury rather than a rave. Blue mana is visible in drinks and architectural channels. A small silver-haired robed figure at the far end provides the requested Lysanthir presence without overwhelming the interior; fine individual rings/ear details are below reliable reading scale here. No material environment or crowd deviation found.
Continuity notes: Retain the sweeping curved bar on the right, tree-column supports, high glazed star roof, soft violet alcoves and musician seating to the left. Keep drinks magical and the social mood restrained. For closer Lysanthir views, use the supplied individual reference rather than treating tiny anchor facial details as a new design.

Purpose: Explore an exterior coherent with the interior and Elven Heights.
Design notes: Coherent new street entrance with pale carved stone, seamless glass canopy, living-wood arch, low planted edges and elegant adult arrivals. NEON NIRVANA is correctly readable and the curved white bar remains visible inside. Ivory/violet tones and restrained blue routes align with the anchor. Exterior footprint is a useful architectural proposal, with no material blocker.

Purpose: Show the social room beyond the bar without repeating its establishing angle.
Design notes: The ivory bar, grown columns, stars, floating orbs and intimate musicians preserve the venue mood. But this repeats the anchor's exact interior direction and several patron placements, adding a large foreground white arch/counter instead of moving to the established bar side. The added counter risks implying a second bar or changed room geometry. Recompose from beside the existing bar toward seating and musicians with a consistent column arrangement.

Purpose: Deliver the workbook’s required magical-drink study.
Design notes: Distinct no-person still life with a faceted crystal glass, condensation, gold utensil and a contained blue spiral over the curved ivory counter. Living wood and violet seating remain legible behind it. The spiral is dark and strongly outlined rather than brightly luminous, but its blue color and confinement to the liquid are clear. No new creature, label or material continuity problem.

Purpose: Test the room at night from a different perspective.
Design notes: Quiet closing-hour occupancy and contained drink mana fit the brief, with the correct ivory counter, violet alcoves, living columns and star ceiling. The camera, architecture, foreground table and main seated patron are essentially unchanged from the anchor. This is an occupancy variant rather than the requested low view along the bar. Reframe along the existing curved counter without creating new room geometry.

Purpose: Reuse the completed booth-to-bar view with Mia and cyberware-bearing regulars.
Design notes: A warm neighborhood bar with rain outside, amber lights, a blue-mana jukebox and familiar regulars. Mia uses her established identity; cyberware appears among the patrons. Room layout and crowd remain an environment proposal.

Purpose: Deliver the required exterior and connect the bar to Humanity Central.
Design notes: A distinct rainy exterior establishes a modest brick doorway and broad warm window, amber string lights, correctly readable venue sign, mixed-species adults and worn everyday cyberware. Teal rain and plain neighboring facades keep the bar inexpensive and welcoming. The newly inferred frontage is a useful concept rather than a fixed floor plan; no material blocker found.

Purpose: Show the working bar and its personal hospitality at a new angle.
Design notes: Mia keeps her black/teal bob, charcoal top, olive cargos and rag on her own left shoulder, with no visible bodily mana. Her build is slimmer than her short stocky identity reference. This also reproduces the anchor camera and virtually all patron positions rather than the requested closer across-counter viewpoint, merely removing the large sign and adding implants. Keep it as an interior variant; reframe the camera and restore her proportions before promoting it to a distinct character scene.

Purpose: Give the bar a characteristic prop and material close-up.
Design notes: Successful distinct close view of the existing arched wood-and-metal jukebox, diamond grille, attached blue supply conduit, amber string lights, brick, wood trim and small wall snapshots. Stool and drink provide scale without distracting figures. Silhouette and material language retain the interior anchor; no material issue found.

Purpose: Show the social space facing away from the first booth-to-bar view.
Design notes: A useful new view along the rain-streaked window booths with mixed-species adult regulars, warm wood, amber string lights, teal street reflections and varied physically connected blue cyberware. Mia stays outside the crop. The friendly inexpensive atmosphere is preserved, while the inferred booth/window arrangement remains an exploratory floor-plan proposal. No material blocker found.

View: 1. Doorway to the hearth and taps
Purpose: Establish a dwarf-scaled modern craft-beer bar.
Design notes: The low timber beams, stone hearth, oak-and-iron bar and blue rune taps are preserved. Borin now has a right-only brass prosthesis with blue wrist vials and a biological left hand. Fine beard details in this wide environment shot are guided by his separate identity reference.

View: 2. A warm door off the factory lane
Purpose: Explore the bar entrance in its industrial neighborhood.
Design notes: Low stone-and-timber frontage carries the carved Iron Spirits sign, warm windows and visible rune taps into a brick industrial lane. Workwear, lunch tins, mature dwarf proportions and distinct blue-linked prosthetic and ear hardware fit the brief.
Continuity notes: The unseen frontage is an exploratory extension of the anchor materials.

Purpose: Show the bar’s social space beyond the counter.
Design notes: Warm hearth, memorial rings, sturdy tables and modern cyberware read well, but this reproduces the anchor doorway composition almost exactly instead of moving beside the bar to explore the hearth gathering.
Continuity notes: Room materials and fixtures remain recognizable; the main issue is insufficiently distinct composition.

Purpose: Deliver the required close view and establish distinctive beer hardware.
Design notes: Strong brass, iron, droplets and pewter close study with physically routed blue mana and a hearth glimpse. The taps are redesigned as large cylindrical rune collars and curved spouts, replacing the anchor's rectangular rune plates and small lever taps.
Continuity notes: Resolve the tap hardware design before treating this close-up as the same established wall.

Purpose: Explore an alternate interior angle and evening occupancy.
Design notes: Quiet last-round occupancy, coats, warm hearth and cold street are effective. The proposed reverse view keeps the bar on the right and relocates the hearth onto the left side wall, rather than preserving the anchor's rear hearth and doorway/bar relationship.
Continuity notes: Room geography needs reconciliation with the anchor before this becomes a continuous interior.

Purpose: Establish the bathhouse architecture and the source of glowing water.
Design notes: Tiered pale stone pools, glowing blue rune-water channels, carved living-wood lattice and a high glazed dome establish a quiet elven bathhouse. Sparse adult bathers and attendants keep relaxation and architecture central. Small STILL WATER and SILENCE KEPT plaques fit the source direction.
Continuity notes: Retain circular pool tiers, wood lattice arches, blue channel intersections and the glazed dome; avoid forcing crowds into private alcove views.

Purpose: Explore arrival and the transition from high-tech city to stillness.
Design notes: Pale marble colonnade and living-wood lattice frame a quiet entrance under the recognizable ribbed dome. Three robed adults, discreet access pedestal and blue floor channels preserve the bathhouse's restrained modern elven identity.
Continuity notes: Exterior entry geometry is a coherent exploratory extension of the interior.

Purpose: Deliver the required private pool and a distinctly smaller spatial concept.
Design notes: An empty foreground alcove basin is screened by grown lattice, with a single local lantern, robe hook and silver water fitting. Marble veining and submerged blue channels match the main room; its dome and terraces remain visible beyond.
Continuity notes: The composition remains close to the anchor axis, but the screened pool provides a distinct private-space detail.

Purpose: Study how water, stone and mana integrate.
Design notes: Clear stepped-water detail shows the small cascade, underwater rune cuts, marble veins and silver fittings; a living-wood screen ties the close view to the venue. Blue light originates in physical channels rather than a floating aura.

Purpose: Test the room in a quiet evening mood.
Design notes: Darkened dome, robed guests and towel preparation provide the evening mood, with the established ivory pools and blue channels intact. The camera and pool layout duplicate the anchor entrance view instead of delivering the requested higher-terrace composition.
Continuity notes: Architecture is continuous; the material issue is repetition of the establishing composition.

Purpose: Establish the landmark silhouette seen throughout Elven Heights.
Design notes: The faceted sunset-lit dome has a strong silhouette above Neonix, reached by an elevated curving garden walkway. Planted foreground, pale stone and restrained blue utility lighting match Elven Heights. Main plaque wording is correct. The interior is intentionally only glimpsed here.
Continuity notes: Preserve large triangular glazing, pale drum base, pointed entrance and sinuous timber approach over the lower city.

Purpose: Show arrival at human scale without losing landmark scale.
Design notes: Low approach emphasizes the white ring wall and silver-ribbed crystal facets, with living-wood paths visible through the gate. Quiet visitors, mature dwarf proportions and connected blue prosthetic hardware fit the modern botanical setting.
Continuity notes: The entrance is elaborated at foundation level; its exact doorway geometry remains an exploratory detail.

Purpose: Deliver the required interior and the scale of its botanical world.
Design notes: Raised curving walkways reveal a tall interior canopy and tiny visitors below. Glass-like leaves, blue plant veins, iridescent birds and the faceted envelope provide a distinct botanical world while preserving the anchor's material language.

Purpose: Study unique botanical materials and their controlled magic.
Design notes: Close glass-leaf branches, blue-veined ferns and one iridescent bird are crisp and organic. The curving wood walkway, white foundation and silver dome ribs remain recognizable behind the foliage.

Purpose: Test the landmark exterior at night and its relation to Neonix.
Design notes: The night exterior gives a distinct oblique view along the white ring foundation, with crisp silver facets, softly lit canopy, tiny walkway visitors and distant Elven Heights spires. Blue plant light and restrained prism tints preserve the botanical identity without turning the dome into an opaque glowing sphere.
Continuity notes: The curving outer walkway and lower arcade are exploratory additions around the established dome silhouette.

View: 1. The great hall of stone and light
Purpose: Establish cathedral-scale knowledge architecture.
Design notes: A convincing long stone-arched library nave pairs carved timber shelves with a blue holographic lineage tree and quiet readers. The main inscription is correct. The hologram contains conspicuous invented labels and a literal BLUE label beside the foreground reader; these need lettering cleanup and do not establish names or lore.
Continuity notes: Keep vaulted pale stone, dark carved shelves, warm alcove lamps and the rooted holographic tree. Do not reuse generated lineage labels as canon.

Purpose: Explore how the old institution meets the modern borough.
Design notes: Ancient round stone portal, carved oak doors and slim blue projection rails connect a modern city street to the warm shelf nave. The entrance inscription is readable and the sparse scholarly population preserves institutional calm.

Purpose: Deliver the required archivist scene without inventing family history.
Design notes: The rotunda, unnamed elven archivist, carved shelves and floating books provide the required medium-wide scene. Several central lineage-tree plaques retain large invented readable labels instead of the requested abstract unnamed nodes.
Continuity notes: Architecture and projection hardware are coherent; remove the readable tree labels before using this as a genealogy-neutral scene.

Purpose: Specify the old/new technology junction at shelf scale.
Design notes: A worn closed codex floats over an illuminated silver rail beside carved oak and a warm reading lamp, matching the intended material study. The literal floating word BLUE remains behind the book and reads as a generation annotation.
Continuity notes: The object and architecture match; the color-label artifact needs cleanup.

Purpose: Explore the private reading experience within the monumental building.
Design notes: Warm reading lamps and night lighting preserve the library mood, but this repeats the anchor entrance-to-rotunda camera rather than looking out from a recessed alcove. It also retains a floating BLUE annotation beside the foreground reader.
Continuity notes: The repeated wide composition does not provide the intended distinct private reading viewpoint.

Purpose: Establish stacked density, commerce and the market’s slightly predatory energy.
Design notes: Crowded layered cyberware stalls, overhead cables and covered balconies create a dense lived-in market. The large TECHTOWN MARKETPLACE and CHROME 4 LESS signs read correctly; mixed adult shoppers and visible implants support everyday technology. Minor incidental sign lettering remains draft detail.
Continuity notes: Retain narrow covered circulation, cyan stall lighting, amber food carts, magenta signs and stacked upper walkways.

Purpose: Show the street approach and vertical stall structure.
Design notes: The large worn parking-structure arch opens into the same dense covered aisle. Stacked timber stalls, tarps, delivery drones, food carts and mixed adult customers keep the improvised commercial energy; the main market sign is clear.

Purpose: Deliver the required intimate stall with arms and eyes on display.
Design notes: Distinct customer-scale counter scene has a vendor bargaining with a dwarf and elf, manufactured ocular modules, prosthetic arms and connected blue cyberware. The foreground mana cartridges carry conspicuous literal BLUE color labels, which read as prompt-derived lettering and need cleanup.

View: 4. A patched arm on the test rig
Purpose: Study affordable everyday technology as a physical object.
Design notes: The worn brass-and-steel arm fills a plausible testing cradle, with inspection glass, visible blue channels, repair marks and a gloved hand using a tool. The recognizable tarped market aisle supplies useful environmental context without a diagram.

Purpose: Explore the market’s upper level and circulation.
Design notes: An upper metal walkway gives a distinct diagonal view across stacked stalls into the crowded aisle. Concrete supports, cable bundles, a parcel drone, amber food steam and varied physical cyberware preserve the market's identity.

Purpose: Establish the required monument, paving and large civic gathering.
Design notes: Five intertwined monument figures, festival stalls, a performance stage and a mixed crowd give the plaza a welcoming civic identity. The required slogan is readable. Five-color organization is stronger on the surrounding facades than on the paving, which should be made clearer in a later refinement.
Continuity notes: Keep the five-figure sculptural cluster and open festival circulation; ground-level views should clarify the five paving colors rather than introduce a different monument.

Purpose: Show the public entrance and its connection to Humanity Central.
Design notes: The same five-figure monument, colorful paving and festival setting are retained, but the entire elevated anchor composition is essentially repeated with new buildings framing its edges. It does not provide the requested eye-level arrival from a street.

View: 3. At the feet of the five figures
Purpose: Deliver the required ground-level monument view.
Design notes: The ground-level base, mixed festivalgoers and five paving colors are clear. The top of the sculpture is cropped, hiding the upper figure and cutting other heads, so the requested complete five-figure monument cannot be read clearly.

Purpose: Study the symbolic design through material and scale.
Design notes: Close plinth study clearly shows all five colored stone rays, the exact Unity plaque, weathered stone and continuous blue channels. Passing adults and visible mechanical footwear provide scale while the established statue's lower forms remain recognizable.

Purpose: Test the plaza at low occupancy while retaining the landmark.
Design notes: Post-festival volunteers fold coverings and small groups linger under warm lanterns. The recognizable five-figure sculpture and now-exposed five-color paving create a useful quiet occupancy variant with an open civic mood.
Continuity notes: The scene keeps the anchor's principal axis despite framing it from a stage edge.

View: 1. The quad from the main gate
Purpose: Establish old brick scholarship joined to advanced research.
Design notes: The main gate frames a lively campus quad of ivy-covered brick halls, modern glass research towers and enclosed skybridges. Adult students, outdoor teaching and physically routed blue utilities make the old/new contrast clear. Gate wording matches the brief; no castle styling.
Continuity notes: Retain brick gables, glass research volumes, the gate arch, intersecting lawn paths and blue-conduit skybridges.

Purpose: Show arrival and the campus relationship to the surrounding city.
Design notes: Ivy-covered brick halls, glass research towers, blue conduit skybridges, readable university gate and mixed adult students remain coherent. The composition and nearly every major figure repeat the anchor exactly rather than showing a new pavement approach.
Continuity notes: Continuity is strong, but this supplies almost no additional location coverage.

Purpose: Deliver the required cluttered lab while preserving the named character.
Design notes: Cluttered laboratory benches, housed mana coils, worn notebooks, instruments and chalkboards establish a clear research interior. Lena retains her tired face, heavy glasses, stylus-held ash-blonde bun, green cardigan and left-only exposed blue mechanical arm consistent with her reference.
Continuity notes: The windows reuse the anchor courtyard vista, while the substantial laboratory foreground supplies a distinct functional space.

Purpose: Study the school’s visual mix of physical and holographic research.
Design notes: The empty bench detail clearly connects an enclosed blue coil, routed cables, sensor equipment and restrained display to an ivy-lined red-brick window and glass tower outside. Chalkboard markings remain abstract; the worn tools and papers make the small research station believable.

Purpose: Explore campus circulation and an alternate evening atmosphere.
Design notes: Warm evening windows and varied adult students supply a convincing campus mood, but the camera repeats the exterior anchor view with a new open glass-railed bridge stretched across the foreground. It does not deliver the requested eye-level view from inside an established enclosed skybridge.
Continuity notes: The added bridge crosses directly above the entrance wall and needs a spatial continuity decision before acceptance.

Purpose: Establish the immense foundry scale and controlled heat.
Design notes: A giant suspended crucible mid-pour dominates the working foundry, with riveted structure, knotwork furnace housings and blue rune pipes. Helmeted workers, separated catwalks and visible safety notices support an industrial workplace. Furnace heat and scale are clear.
Continuity notes: Retain heavy arched hall, overhead crane rails, shielded furnace line and guarded walkways; PPE remains part of the workers' design.

View: 2. The industrial gate at shift change
Purpose: Explore the foundry exterior and district-scale silhouette.
Design notes: Broad brick-and-riveted-iron frontage, tall smoking stacks, massive knotwork lintel and overhead freight cranes carry the foundry identity outside. Worker circulation is separated from the raised cargo rails, with adult dwarf and human arrivals and distinct blue-linked industrial implants.
Continuity notes: The cliffside exterior and entry arrangement are exploratory extensions of the anchor industrial hall.

Purpose: Deliver the required worker-scale view of skilled furnace control.
Design notes: An adult dwarven operator in visor, gloves and apron reads a large blue rune gauge inside a glazed control station. Worn brass instruments, contained mana and the recognizable furnace and crane beyond the glass make a clear protected working environment.
Continuity notes: The background repeats the anchor hall angle, but the control-room foreground supplies the requested distinct environmental focus.

Purpose: Specify how dwarven craft and mana regulate heavy industry.
Design notes: A large brass inspection seal, blue embedded channels, carved knotwork, rivets and soot provide a strong furnace material study. The protective railing and small background workers establish scale, with orange heat confined behind the heavy housing.
Continuity notes: The circular seal and adjoining plate are a new detail proposal using the established furnace materials; the distant sloped housing remains recognizable.

Purpose: Test architecture and circulation with a quieter production state.
Design notes: The stopped crucible, reduced orange heat, clearer blue runes and small inspection crews convincingly show a pause between pours. The image nevertheless reproduces the anchor camera and furnace arrangement almost exactly instead of delivering the requested reverse maintenance-gallery view.
Continuity notes: Strong fixture continuity; the material issue is repeated establishing coverage.

Purpose: Establish a subterranean craft complex with depth and activity.
Design notes: A carved subterranean tunnel recedes past warm individual workshop alcoves, compact mature artisans and a narrow materials rail. Blue rune bands and small cyberware touches connect craft to Neonix. The main MADE BY HAND sign is readable and the space feels inhabited rather than a dungeon.
Continuity notes: Retain stone barrel arches, repeated working alcoves, warm forge pools, restrained blue rune borders and the central trolley route.

Purpose: Explore the entrance and relation to the Dwarf District.
Design notes: Stone stairs and worn handrails descend beside a practical freight lift into a rune-lit rock arch beneath brick foundations. Adult craftworkers carry closed tool cases past warm workshop alcoves, giving a clear modern working transition underground.
Continuity notes: The camera looks down the descent rather than from its lower end; the new entrance geometry remains a coherent exploratory extension of the established carved-stone tunnels.

Purpose: Reveal one functional workspace off the main tunnel.
Design notes: A nearer workshop alcove reveals mature dwarf artisans, a vented forge, anvils, tool racks and a modern magnifying lamp over a decorated blade bench. Contained blue etching equipment and varied mechanical ear, eye and arm fittings preserve the modern craft setting.
Continuity notes: The recurring carved arches, rune strips and ore rails remain visible beyond, while the bench and forge give the view a distinct functional focus.

Purpose: Deliver the required close view of craftsmanship and materials.
Design notes: Rough ornamental metal, a leather pad, wrapped grip sample, scattered engraving tools and warm stone forge create a useful close material study. The large powered etching stylus appears to hover unsupported with its tip against glowing blade runes, undermining the requested inactive still-life with tools set aside.
Continuity notes: Resolve the tool support or lay it down before treating this as a physically coherent bench detail.

Purpose: Test another time and a more intimate sense of the complex.
Design notes: The quiet tunnel, ore carts, portable tool racks and artisans closing up communicate after-hours work clearly. However, the repeated oversized iron doors with barred viewing slots read as cell doors, conflicting with the requested dwarf-scaled workshop entries and explicit direction to avoid a prison or dungeon appearance.
Continuity notes: Stone vaults, blue runes and warm door seams match the anchor; the new workshop-door design needs reconciliation.

Purpose: Establish the stadium bowl and dwarven identity at full crowd scale.
Design notes: Revised from an uppermost grandstand: a broad multi-tier stadium bowl, thousands of tiny spectators, monumental stone-and-steel supports and tiny mechs on the distant arena floor now establish the required major venue scale. Blue electric floodlights and clan knotwork retain the dwarf industrial identity.

Purpose: Explore public arrival and the exterior mass.
Design notes: Inspected against stonehall-stadium-location-01-v3. A distinct street-level arrival view with a monumental carved gate, dwarven reliefs, ticket turnstiles and a varied adult crowd. The exact STONEHALL STADIUM lettering is integrated into the gate. Heavy stone, knotwork columns and riveted iron arches convincingly extend the anchor's architecture; red/gold banners and physically routed blue conduits fit the brief. No visible palette values, BLUE labels or external captions. The tight crop establishes gate height more clearly than the full low, broad exterior mass, but supplies useful new exterior coverage.
Continuity notes: The unseen exterior is a coherent exploratory proposal. Warm exterior floodlights differ from the anchor's blue interior light without breaking the material palette; blue conduits remain visible. Full exterior footprint and roof span cannot be verified from this crop.

Purpose: Deliver the required smaller competition and contrast with mechs.
Design notes: Two mature dwarf wrestlers, a referee, close spectators and a compact recessed sand pit successfully distinguish the smaller sport from the mech arena. Clothing, anatomy, heavy stone edges and connected blue cyberware are readable, with no gore or stray palette/BLUE labels. The camera is elevated above the pit rather than at the requested ground level. The centered distant stadium, sign, roof opening and paired floodlights repeat the anchor's framing closely, so this provides new activity more strongly than a new spatial view.
Continuity notes: The distant bowl preserves the v3 anchor's massive crowd scale, carved columns and iron roof supports. The foreground pit reads as an inserted terrace beside or above the main bowl, but its floor connection and circulation are not established. Retain as a useful wrestling concept pending a clearer ground-level angle or an explicit spatial placement for this smaller pit.

Purpose: Study the construction and technology that define the arena.
Design notes: A genuinely distinct upper-tier detail: worn stone steps and a practical handrail lead past a riveted curved iron support, red/gold banner and the rear of a suspended floodlight. A bright blue conduit visibly enters the light housing. The tiny mech bout and dense distant spectators preserve the v3 anchor's stadium scale. No visible palette values, BLUE labels, sponsor brands or external captions. The banner includes large rune-like letterforms around a bear emblem; they are not readable ordinary words, but simpler abstract ornament would follow the no-new-slogans direction more closely.
Continuity notes: Curved roof brackets, carved pillars, knotwork tier fascia, the open roof and polygonal arena boundary remain recognizable from v3. This is useful material and infrastructure coverage rather than another full-bowl composition. The specific banner emblem is an exploratory design, not an established clan identity.

Purpose: Show the monumental architecture during a quiet reset.
Design notes: The floor-level upward view delivers an empty, calm arena with four maintenance workers, dimmer blue-mana floodlights and red/gold banners. The people remain small relative to the overall structure, and the intact stone bowl reads as a working venue after a competition. No visible palette values, BLUE labels or extra readable signage. The lower camera and vacant seating provide distinct coverage despite retaining the anchor's centered symmetry.
Continuity notes: The v3 open roof, curved iron brackets, carved supporting columns, tier fascia and far entrance are retained. Empty stands expose relatively few broad seating rows, making the capacity read less emphatically as tens of thousands than the densely populated anchor; refinement should reconcile seating density and tier dimensions before these images become a fixed architectural plan. This remains a useful quiet-state concept rather than a verified exact reconstruction.

Purpose: Establish the maze as a dense lived-in network.
Design notes: Successful elevated rope-bridge view over dense occupied alleys, container stalls, connected metal stairs, food steam, wet paving and warm doorways. The blue/cyan, magenta and acid-green circuit-like mural paths give a distinctive network read; mutants remain people. THE NEON LABYRINTH main sign is correct. Material signage issue: the prominent vertical sign beside it reads NEOMIX, an unintended readable city-like name. Remove or abstract this extra label before propagating the anchor. Smaller invented shop marks should stay non-readable. The mural concept is very literal circuitry; later detail views should also show layered figurative street art and visibly BLUE mana rather than establishing magenta/green energy as universal mana colors.
Continuity notes: Preserve three-to-four-storey alley depth, bolted container stalls, metal stair runs, rope bridges and inhabited food-stall junctions. Do not carry the NEOMIX lettering into followers or canon. Other colored paint/light can remain decorative while blue is the mana route.

Purpose: Show the public approach and the spatial choice at its threshold.
Design notes: The welded scrap arch opens onto two active alley branches, with stacked containers, food steam, bridges and ordinary mutant residents. A useful closer arrival view that preserves the cyan depth and magenta/green mural language.

Purpose: Deliver the required nightlife view at street level.
Design notes: A lively music-doorway crowd, descending metal steps and warm skewer stall provide a distinct social view. Contemporary clothing, varied adult bodies and connected blue cyberware remain consistent with the neighborhood.

Purpose: Study the defining mural magic and urban reuse.
Design notes: Close layered murals, patched brick and metal, paint tools, candles and an anonymous artist with a mechanical arm successfully show the lived-in detail. Blue painted channels connect the mural to the established visual language without invented memorial text.

View: 5. The maze from the middle bridge
Purpose: Explore traversal from a new height without changing the established network.
Design notes: A diagonal view down from a metal bridge/stair landing reveals the connected alley junction, food stall, hanging walkways and blue paths. The camera is on metal rather than the requested rope bridge, but adds a useful complementary view of the same dense environment.

View: 1. White facade in the neon district
Purpose: Establish the required clean island within the Mutant Quarters.
Design notes: Strong small white/chrome clinic facade inserted among dark graffiti-covered brick tenements. Cocoon-shaped frosted entrance, cold clean interior light, one morpho-blue arch accent and dignified varied mutant adults in a hopeful queue match the brief. THE CHRYSALIS CLINIC and BECOME. are spelled correctly. Interior equipment is recognizable; blue mana routed through it is subdued, and common bodily cyberware in the queue is not clearly legible at this scale. The scene remains clinical without gore or horror. Suitable environment concept with technology-detail emphasis needed in the suite/pod followers.
Continuity notes: Keep the low white facade, segmented cocoon entry, thin chrome bands and single morpho-blue accent. The street-facing room can remain a front care/preparation area; do not infer that private surgery must be exposed to the street. Named Nova Seraph is not identifiable here, so her later suite must use her dedicated reference. Make blue-mana equipment conduits and modest everyday cyberware clearer in closer scenes.

Purpose: Show the transition between street and care.
Design notes: The cocoon-shaped frosted doors, white/chrome waiting area, old brick edges and restrained blue accents match the clinic. Three adult patients with distinct physiologies and everyday cyberware give a calm threshold scene.

Purpose: Deliver the required named surgeon scene while keeping it calm and non-graphic.
Design notes: Nova retains the platinum buzz cut, serene face, white suit and exactly two additional shoulder-blade arms, clearly separate from her natural arms and ceiling equipment. The draped patient is non-graphic. The suite is placed directly beside an open street entrance; refine the floor plan and privacy to make it read as a protected interior treatment room.

Purpose: Study the clinic’s hopeful technology at a human scale.
Design notes: An empty pearl-white recovery chair behind frosted cocoon screens provides a distinct equipment and material study. Chrome fittings, small blue conduits and exposed old brick keep the converted clinic identity without horror apparatus.

Purpose: Explore the social room from the inside looking out.
Design notes: The pale waiting room, diverse adult patients and understated blue cyberware work well. The reverse view repeats an exterior clinic facade and cocoon entrance beyond the interior doorway, creating an uncertain floor plan. Keep the patient/material ideas but reconcile the entrance direction with the anchor.

Purpose: Establish the converted warehouse as a bold performance venue.
Design notes: Distinct converted brick warehouse with iron structural bands/trusses, lit wraparound marquee, wet neon street and a lively costumed crowd of varied adult mutant forms. The marquee accurately carries THE FRINGE THEATRE and TONIGHT: SKIN, A REVUE across its two faces. Warm gold/magenta theatrical light and visible tiered seating support an intimate unconventional venue; no red-velvet palace or horror treatment. Cybernetic costume/armor shapes are visible but blue-mana links are not prominent in this exterior. Keep readable peripheral poster scribbles as incidental unapproved graphics rather than new shows or lore.
Continuity notes: Retain the tall arched warehouse windows, iron columns, open double doorway, projecting corner marquee and compact tiered room. Later performance/detail views should show scaffold seating, the mirrored platform and clear blue-mana stage conduits. Exterior costume choices do not establish named characters or faction affiliation.

Purpose: Show entrance scale and the venue’s repurposed structure.
Design notes: The closer marquee approach retains rough brick, riveted warehouse supports, a simple ticket table and varied adult patrons. The mirrored platform and blue light cables glimpsed inside connect arrival to the performance space.

Purpose: Deliver the required stage view and avant-garde spatial concept.
Design notes: A small scaffold-seated audience faces mutant performers and a visibly rigged aerialist above a mirrored platform. Magenta/gold stage haze, scrap light structures and exposed iron trusses preserve the intimate experimental warehouse theatre.

Purpose: Study the theatre’s distinctive set materials and stage technology.
Design notes: Close repaired mirror seams, a sculptural scrap light support and a stagehand's gloved hand explain the theatre's handmade blue-mana equipment. Distinct detail composition with the same brick and truss vocabulary.

View: 5. The empty room after the revue
Purpose: Test the performance space as architecture after the crowd disperses.
Design notes: A quiet reverse view from the mirrored stage shows empty scaffold seating and three crew resetting props. Dim gold work lamps and fine blue power lines make a useful after-show counterpart without turning the venue into an ornate opera house.

Purpose: Establish vast organized reuse and the signature greenhouse.
Design notes: Organized material-sorted scrap mounds, navigable working lanes, sheds assembled from salvaged doors/car panels, magnet crane and green planted greenhouse create a resourceful working yard. Respirators, ordinary labor and practical blue-mana prosthetics preserve residents' dignity; main THE BONEYARD — NOTHING IS TRASH wording is accurate. Grey-violet air and low orange sun fit. The greenhouse is present, but regular rectangular glazing makes the required reused windshields less specific than intended; the planned greenhouse detail should clarify curved, mismatched windshield panels. Foreground cyberware is brighter cyan than the intended dim Gloom-grey, a refinement note rather than a change to the environment's layout.
Continuity notes: Keep sorted metal/glass/vehicle-part hills, door-panel sheds, central cart lanes and the crane behind the greenhouse. Preserve the greenhouse's position while clarifying windshield reuse in closer views. Dim its residents' mana toward grey-blue when feasible. No foreground figure is approved as Rollo; his shed view must use his dedicated reference.

Purpose: Show entry and an understandable organization of the salvage yard.
Design notes: Sorted salvage lanes, greenhouse and subdued palette match the anchor, but the salvaged car-door sign is implausibly oversized beside people and sheds. The camera and background largely repeat the anchor instead of the requested eye-level gate approach.

Purpose: Deliver the required interior of sorted parts with the established character.
Design notes: Strong organized jar-filled shed and gentle sorting action; bald head, goggles, beard and patched exoskeleton outfit read as Rollo. His broad heavy build is reduced, and the armored boot appears on his right foot instead of the reference left; restore the established body and asymmetry.

Purpose: Study the landmark and the yard’s environmental ingenuity.
Design notes: Distinct closer greenhouse composition with reused glazing, condensation, moss trays, irrigation and a respirator-wearing caretaker. Sorted salvage and patched sheds preserve the anchor materials and working-yard context.

View: 5. Crane rails through the sorted hills
Purpose: Show movement and the yard’s scale from ground level.
Design notes: Readable crane rail corridor, material-sorted hills, distant greenhouse and subdued sunset retain place continuity. Crews remain beside the tracks and clear of the empty magnet; carts are open rather than the requested closed design, a minor detail.

Purpose: Establish the underground market and lantern-open convention.
Design notes: Coherent storm-drain market with arched cracked concrete, crate/tarp stalls, central flowing channel and dry raised walking margins. Dim grey-blue lanterns and modest blue-cyberware links suit the subdued palette; respirator-wearing adults bargain normally. BREATHLESS BAZAAR — MASKS ON, MOUTHS SHUT wording is accurate, although displayed on a hanging board rather than chalk at the mouth. The established tunnel is broader and more sparsely occupied than the low crowded source description. Those scale/occupancy refinements can be addressed by lower closer follower cameras and fuller active-stall scenes without losing the usable structural anchor. A specific unlit lantern at a closed stall is not clearly demonstrated here.
Continuity notes: Keep the central water channel, raised dry margins, repeated arched concrete, patched tarps and physically hung grey-blue mana lanterns. In the lantern detail explicitly pair a lit/open stall with an unlit/closed stall. Do not transform the market into a colorful bazaar or infer Ivor's identity from anonymous vendors. The entrance follower should restore chalk signage at the tunnel mouth.

Purpose: Show the discreet public approach and descent.
Design notes: Distinct service-passage entrance with chalk warning, raised dry walkway, steps, rusted rail and dim lanterns. Respirator-wearing customers and a quiet lookout fit the restrained tunnel setting.

Purpose: Deliver the required medicine stall and recognizable trader.
Design notes: Ivor retains the recognizable hat, ashen face, lowered brass respirator and coat, with sparse filters and used tech at his stall. However, the image repeats the anchor-wide tunnel composition almost exactly; move closer to the requested customer-eye medium-wide stall view so his identity details are legible.

Purpose: Study the market’s unique communication through a prop.
Design notes: Good close lantern, filter and damp-concrete detail, but the neighboring shuttered tarp stalls also have visibly glowing lanterns. Extinguish the neighboring lantern to preserve the required lit-open/unlit-closed signal.

View: 5. At the junction beneath the city
Purpose: Explore market circulation and varied tunnel depth.
Design notes: Distinct two-branch junction with dry connected walkways, central drainage channels and small bridges. Crate-and-tarp stalls, restrained grey-blue lanterns, respirators and a wall-side lookout preserve the anchor setting without blocking circulation.

Purpose: Establish the park’s melancholy beauty and artificial haze.
Design notes: Gentle melancholy park with lamp-lined paths, bare ribbon-tied trees, sparse residents, fairy lights, gazebo and dry fountain. Soft grey-violet atmosphere, warm gold lamp halos and faint blue ground mist match the source, and THE VEIL OF MIST is correct. No horror staging. Foreground clothes lean toward fantasy-adventure silhouettes, and the artificial mist machinery is not visible; these weaken the urban Neonix reading but the distinctive park architecture and mood are usable. Do not interpret this as a forest outside the city or make the ribbons into newly named lore.
Continuity notes: Preserve old iron lamps/gazebo, the small dry fountain, curving paths, dead ribbon-bearing trees and restrained blue mist. Add visible salvaged vent fittings in the planned detail view and practical worn city clothing/respirators with occasional modest cyberware in closer people scenes. Avoid propagating armor-like wardrobe as the general Plagued uniform; no universal eye treatment is established.

Purpose: Show arrival from the Gloomscape into a softer public place.
Design notes: Gate, concrete city edge, ribbons, respirator-wearing arrivals and luminous park mist fit the requested entrance. Remove the clearly printed prompt metadata beneath the nameplate: Place; context: The Gloomscape.

Purpose: Deliver the required intimate respite scene.
Design notes: Affectionate adult couple, respirators, worn layers and gentle lamp light work well. The entire park background and camera repeat the anchor with a bench inserted; reframe nearer the bench to deliver the requested distinct medium-wide companionship view.

Purpose: Study the park’s emotional detail and artificial mechanism.
Design notes: Faded tied ribbons, fairy lights and a maintained mist vent are clearly shown in a distinct detail view. The prominent lamp shaft deforms into a hooked, split-looking section instead of a coherent iron post; repair its structure. Three extra residents also distract from the requested object detail.

Purpose: Explore the wider park layout beyond the main path.
Design notes: Warm lamps, ribbons, restrained mist and sparse residents preserve the atmosphere, but the anchor gazebo and fountain remain in the background while a second gazebo frame and fountain are inserted in front. Recompose from the established gazebo without duplicating these landmarks.
